name: Eyal Ofer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Eyal Ofer is the chairman of the Monaco-based Ofer Global, active in shipping, real estate, technology, banking, energy and other investments.
Ofer is one of two sons of shipping magnate Sammy Ofer, who died in 2011 and was once Israel's richest man.
The elder Ofer brother has expanded these holdings significantly. Through Zodiac Group, his shipping company, he now owns and operates roughly 200 ships.
His Global Holdings real estate portfolio spans 120 properties around the world, including 15 Central Park West and 50 United Nations Plaza in Manhattan, and Vogue House in London.
Eyal's other assets include the VC tech fund O.G. Venture Partners, O.G. Energy and stakes in the public companies Mizrahi Tefahot Bank and Royal Caribbean Cruises.
He and his family also started the Eyal & Marilyn Ofer Family Foundation, which supports education, healthcare and the arts.
forbes_facts: Eyal and his brother Idan split their father's art holdings, a rare collection rumored to include pieces by Van Gogh and Picasso.
Ofer's four children--Daniel, Jonathan, David and Olivia--are all involved in the various divisions of Ofer Global.

name: Renata Kellnerova
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2023)
forbes_bio: Renata Kellnerova is the widow of Petr Kellner, the former richest person in the Czech Republic, who died in March 2021 at age 56.
Kellner died in a helicopter crash in Alaska during a heliskiing trip.
Kellnerova and her three daughters control PFF Group, the $44 billion (assets) conglomerate with interests in telecommunications, media, financial services and real estate.
She chairs The Kellner Family Foundation, which focuses on education.

name: Alexander Gerko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Alex Gerko, a former FX quant trader for Deutsche Bank and head of FX trading of GSA Capital, founded algorithmic trading company XTX Markets in 2015.
Gerko is Co-CEO of XTX, which posted record profits in 2021 and became the largest emerging market FX provider in 2022.
Born in Russia, he has lived and worked in the U.K. since 2006 and has U.K. citizenship.
Gerko has invested in 64 companies including Compology, provider of artificial intelligence solutions in waste and transportation and Yet Analytics as an angel investor, according to Pitchbook.
XTX, which paid dividends of more than $1 billion to Gerko in 2022, sued Trump's former accounting firm, Mazars, after it refused to work with its Russian-born owner.
forbes_facts: Gerko has PhD in Mathematics and wrote several research papers including one that tested market timing for trading.
After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, XTX issued a statement in support of Ukraine and donated more than $25 million to nonprofits providing humanitarian relief.

name: J. Joe Ricketts
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1999-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Online stock trading pioneer Joe Ricketts founded brokerage firm Ameritrade five decades ago in Omaha, Nebraska and took it public in 1997.
His company acquired TD Waterhouse for $2.9 billion in stock and cash in 2006 and renamed itself TD Ameritrade.
In 2019, competitor Charles Schwab announced it would acquire TD Ameritrade in a $26 billion deal.
Ricketts retired from the board of directors of TD Ameritrade in 2011 but remained its largest individual shareholder until it was acquired.
In 2014, he funded the construction of religious silent retreat center, the Cloisters on the Platte, in Nebraska.
His four children are the majority owners of the Chicago Cubs, which won the World Series in 2016 for the first time in 108 years.
forbes_facts: It took Ricketts nine years to graduate from Creighton University because he periodically had to stop and earn money to pay his tuition.
Ricketts' son, Pete, was sworn in as a US. senator from Nebraska in 2023 and previously served as governor of the state.

name: Tanya Saadé Zeenny
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Tanya Saadé Zeenny is the daughter of late shipping magnate Jacques Saadé, who died in 2018.
Jacques founded CMA CGM, now one of the world's largest shipping companies, in Marseille, France in 1978.
Tanya jointly controls the company with her siblings, Rodolphe Saadé and Jacques Saadé Jr., as well as her mother Naila.
In 1995, Tanya set up CMA CGM's communications department. She now heads the company's corporate social responsibility department and the CMA CGM Foundation.
The $55.5 billion (2024 revenues) company operates more than 700 vessels, serving 420 commercial ports in 160 countries.

name: Ge Li

WuXi AppTec was formally known as Wuxi PharmaTech
Li also chairs WuXi Biologics, a global open-access biologics technology platform company
A subsidiary of WuXi AppTec broke ground on a 190 acre pharmaceutical campus in Delaware in August 2022.
Li holds a Ph.D. degree in organic chemistry from Columbia University
forbes_facts: The Ge Li & Ning Zhao Family Foundation donated $20 million to Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York in 2020 to help fight lung cancer.

name: Dan Kurzius
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Dan Kurzius founded what later became Mailchimp with Ben Chestnut in 2001 as a side project to their web design company.
Mailchimp's email marketing software for small businesses garnered enough customers that in 2007 they committed to it full time.
Wary of giving up control to outside investors, Kurzius and Chestnut bootstrapped growth from profits and took no outside money.
In 2021, Intuit announced it would acquire Mailchimp in a $12 billion cash and stock acquisition.
At the time of announcement, Chestnut and Kurzius each owned 50% of the Atlanta-based company, which had $800 million in 2020 revenue.
forbes_facts: Kurzius was a part-time DJ and competitive skateboarder before getting into web design.
The two cofounders met when Chestnut hired Kurzius to work at Cox Interactive Media's dot-com era MP3 music service.

name: Vikas Oberoi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Property magnate Vikas Oberoi controls and runs Mumbai-listed Oberoi Realty, known for its high-end suburban condos.
Oberoi owns a Westin hotel in suburban Mumbai and is building the city's first Ritz-Carlton hotel and residences.
Oberoi, who is not related to the family behind the Oberoi hotel chain, is also building a mall, hotel and office tower in midtown Mumbai.
The company has leased 1.5 million square feet in its suburban office tower in Mumbai to Morgan Stanley.
forbes_facts: Oberoi is married to Gayatri, a former Bollywood actress.
He has a pilot's license and enjoys flying.
In  2023, Oberoi and his wife were involved in a car crash while holidaying in Italy but survived while two others died.

name: Katharine Rayner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Katharine Rayner  inherited an estimated 17% stake in media and automotive conglomerate Cox Enterprises from her mother, Anne Cox Chambers.
Cox Enterprises, a private communications, media, and automotive conglomerate started by Rayner's grandfather, has $23.1 billion in revenues.
Her siblings, James Chambers and Margaretta Taylor, also inherited an estimated 17% stake each in Cox Enterprises.
Neither Rayner nor her siblings or mother have ever had an active role in the company.
Her cousin, Jim Kennedy, is chairman emeritus of Cox Enterprises. Her nephew, Alex Taylor, is CEO and chairman.
forbes_facts: Rayner lives in East Hampton, N.Y. She is known to be an avid gardener.
A noted philanthropist, she serves on the board of the New York Public Library and the Morgan Library.

name: Joao Moreira Salles
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Joao Moreira Salles is a Brazilian documentary filmmaker and member of one of Brazil's oldest banking families.
His late father, Walther Moreira Salles, was the founder of Unibanco and a former ambassador to the United States.
In 2008 Unibanco merged with Itau, then Brazil's second-largest commercial bank, creating Itau-Unibanco, the largest bank in Latin America.
Moreira Salles and his three brothers, all billionaires, also own stakes in CBMM, the world's leading supplier of the mineral niobium.
forbes_facts: Moreira Salles' 2006 documentary Santiago won the Knight Grand Jury Prize for Documentary Features at the Miami International Film Festival.

name: Eduardo Eurnekian
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Eduardo Eurnekian, the son of Armenian immigrants to Argentina, first operated in the textile industry.
He delved into the cable TV business in the 1980s. In the 1990s, he netted $750 million in the sale of Argentine TV firm Cablevision.
Under his Corporacion America, Eurnekian and partners own 52 airports around the world, with reported revenues of more than $1.4 billion.
In February 2018, Corporacion America Airports went public on the New York Stock Exchange; Eurnekian's nephew, Martin, is CEO.
Compañía General de Combustibles, another of his ventures, is an oil and gas producer in Argentina operating hydrocarbon fields and pipelines.
forbes_facts: In 2011, he sold 21 duty free shops in Argentina, Uruguay, Ecuador and Armenia to Switzerland's Dufry AG for $975 million.
He's never married and has no children.
